ED Clerking - 05/03/2020, 21:22

Presenting complaint: Three-day history of fever, dry cough and shortness of breath in a woman in her 20s-30s.

History: No significant past medical history. Non-smoker. Reports worsening breathlessness over the previous 24 hours with mild pleuritic chest discomfort. No known asthma.

Observations: Temperature 38.4°C, HR 112 bpm, BP 118/70 mmHg, SpO2 90% on air recorded at 11:53 on 05/03/2020, improved to 95% on 2L nasal cannula. NEWS2 score 7.

Swab taken for SARS-CoV-2 PCR at 17:12; result returned positive, reported 18:46 on 05/03/2020.

Examination: Tachypnoeic, reduced air entry at the right lung base with scattered crackles. Otherwise unremarkable examination.

Impression: Confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia with hypoxaemia, high NEWS2.

Plan: Admit for oxygen therapy and monitoring. Referral made to the medical SHO but no record of it being received; re-referred later in the shift. Admitted to hospital at 20:22 on 05/03/2020. VTE risk assessment: high risk, thromboprophylaxis to be prescribed on the ward. Chest X-ray and bloods including FBC, U&E, CRP, D-dimer, LFTs sent. Isolation in side room as per COVID-19 pathway. Escalation to be discussed with the medical team on arrival to the ward.

Ed Clerking
